segments.text: This hormone dies in one hundred twenty seconds. And it quietly powers a multi-billion-dollar drug class. Today we fold it live — with an A.I. agent.

I'm going to show you three things in under two minutes. The biology that actually matters. The engineering pattern you can steal. And a real Boltz prediction with real confidence scores — not a slide deck.

Meet G.L.P. one. Thirty amino acids from your gut. After you eat, it tells the pancreas: release insulin if sugar is high. It also turns down appetite in the brain. Problem? An enzyme called D.P.P. four destroys it in about two minutes.
So medicine needed the same message — in a structure that survives. That's the story behind modern metabolic drugs. Same fold family idea. Engineered half-life measured in days, not minutes.

Now the engineering. Omnigent from Databricks is a meta-harness. You don't rewrite your agent to change models. One Y.A.M.L. file. Swap one line — Claude, Codex, Pi, Grok. Tools and policies stay put.

Look at the real product surface. Shareable sessions. Tool cards that stream as they run. Contextual policies. Agents panel. This is how teams actually collaborate on agent work — not copy-paste from a chat window.

Watch. Sequence in. Boltz cloud. Coordinates out. Our live run: structure confidence zero point eight three. P.L.D.D.T. zero point nine zero. Thirty residues. That is a real prediction artifact, not a mock.
Here is the fold. N to C. Heavy atoms. This is what the agent drops into the workspace — still, spin movie, metrics — ready to share.
If you're in biocomputing: sequence to structure in one session. If you're an engineer: portable agents with guardrails. If you're a tech leader: one layer above the model chaos. That's the value.
Protein Lab on Omnigent. Run it: omni run, agents, protein-lab. Fold the two-minute hormone yourself.
